description: We’re a team of six who love space, design and code. We’re taking on the “Abandoned but not Forgotten” challenge, turning NASA’s history into an interactive 3D experience for kids. Our skills cover research, storytelling, UI/UX design, 3D web development (Three.js) and front-end engineering. Our team is complete, but we’re always happy to connect with fellow space fans!
summary:
What if the machines we've sent into space could tell us their stories?

ASTRAVUM: Echoes of Space is an immersive, interactive storytelling experience that brings humanity's space exploration achievements to life through the voices of the machines that made them possible.

Instead of presenting space technology through traditional facts and technical descriptions, we invite users to embark on a cinematic journey where they encounter spacecraft and scientific instruments, interact with them, and uncover their memories, missions, challenges, and contributions to our understanding of the universe.

Through interactive dialogue, atmospheric sound design, animated environments, and a dynamic journey from individual memories to an orbital perspective, ASTRAVUM transforms scientific exploration into a personal and emotional experience.

Our project addresses the challenge of making space science more accessible, engaging, and meaningful, particularly for younger generations and audiences without technical backgrounds.

We believe the machines that explore the unknown deserve more than a place in history. They deserve to have their stories heard.

ASTRAVUM turns space technology into stories, and stories into inspiration.
details:
ASTRAVUM: Echoes of Space

Every machine sent into space has a story. We wanted to give those stories a voice.

When we started working on ASTRAVUM, we kept coming back to one thought: we hear so much about the discoveries made in space, but rarely think about the machines that made those discoveries possible.

Behind every spacecraft, rover, and scientific instrument is an incredible story of engineering, exploration, challenges, and years of human dedication. Yet, for many people, these stories are often reduced to technical information that can be difficult to connect with.

We wanted to change that.

What We Created

ASTRAVUM is an interactive, story-driven web experience that lets users explore space through the memories of the machines that helped us understand it.

Instead of reading long descriptions or scrolling through facts, users become part of the story.

As they explore the environment, they encounter different machines, interact with them, and gradually discover their memories. Each interaction reveals something about the machine's mission, the challenges it faced, and the role it played in space exploration.

We wanted every encounter to feel like a conversation rather than a lesson.

To make the experience more engaging, we combined storytelling with animations, atmospheric sound, interactive dialogue, and cinematic transitions. Once the memories have been explored, the experience shifts into an orbital perspective, bringing the journey together before the player returns to their spacecraft.

Why We Built It

We believe that curiosity is one of the most powerful ways to learn.

Space science is fascinating, but it can sometimes feel distant or overly complicated, especially for people who don't have a scientific background.

Our goal was to make it feel closer.

By giving these machines personalities and letting them tell their stories, we hope users will remember more than just their names or technical specifications. We want them to understand why their missions mattered and appreciate the people and ideas behind them.

If someone finishes ASTRAVUM feeling curious enough to search for a mission they just experienced, then we have accomplished something meaningful.

How We Developed It

We built ASTRAVUM as a browser-based interactive experience, combining web development, visual design, animation, audio, and narrative writing.

Throughout development, we focused on making the interactions smooth, the storytelling understandable, and the overall experience immersive without making it difficult to navigate.

We used GitHub to manage our project and Vercel to make the final experience accessible online.

We also used AI-assisted development tools, including Claude Code and ChatGPT, to help with coding, debugging, and improving parts of the experience. The concept, creative direction, storytelling decisions, and final implementation were guided and reviewed by our team.

What Makes ASTRAVUM Different?

We didn't want to build another website that simply displays information about space.

We wanted to create something people could experience.

The machines in ASTRAVUM are not just objects on a screen. They are characters with stories worth hearing.

By combining real space exploration concepts with imaginative storytelling, we created a different way for people to connect with science.

And perhaps most importantly, we wanted to remind people that behind every machine exploring the universe, there are humans who once dreamed of reaching it.

ASTRAVUM is our way of making those dreams, discoveries, and stories feel alive again.
